annotations.Question: What is the most common nuclear chromatin pattern in leukemia cells?
annotations.Answer: Open chromatin is the most common nuclear chromatin pattern in leukemia cells. Open chromatin is characterized by loose and diffuse staining of the chromatin, giving the appearance of open spaces within the nucleus. This pattern is seen in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) cells. In contrast, the closed chromatin pattern is seen in reactive lymphoid cells and is not typically seen in leukemia cells.

annotations.Question: What is the most common nuclear shape in leukemia cells?
annotations.Answer: Irregular nuclear shape is the most common nuclear shape in leukemia cells. Irregular nuclear shape is characterized by an abnormal shape of the nucleus, which can be lobulated, indented, or otherwise distorted. This pattern is seen in AML and ALL cells. In contrast, the round nuclear shape is seen in reactive lymphoid cells and is not typically seen in leukemia cells.
